summary.text: Teresa Leger Fernandez is the Democratic incumbent for New Mexico's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2020 and seeking a fourth term.

A Yale and Stanford Law graduate, she worked as an attorney and advocate in New Mexico, ran her own Santa Fe law and strategy firm, and served in presidential appointments under Presidents Clinton and Obama before entering Congress.

paragraphs.text: Leger Fernandez was born in Las Vegas, New Mexico, in 1959 and describes herself as a 17th-generation New Mexican and part of the state's first Head Start class, according to her official House biography.
She is the daughter of a New Mexico state senator and a bilingual educator, per the Albuquerque Journal, and grew up in Las Vegas, New Mexico.
She earned a B.A. from Yale University and a J.D. from Stanford Law School.

After law school, Leger Fernandez worked as an attorney and advocate. Her official biography says she won legal cases on voting rights, tribal sovereignty and acequia water protection and served as an acequia commissioner, and that as a public interest lawyer she helped secure funding for schools, rural health clinics, broadband, affordable housing and infrastructure.
She worked as counsel and a strategist with Leger Law & Strategy.
She served as a White House Fellow working on housing issues (a Clinton appointee) and as vice chair of the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation (an Obama appointee).

Leger Fernandez won the 2020 Democratic primary for the open 3rd District seat against six other Democrats, including state Rep. Joseph Sanchez and author and former CIA officer Valerie Plame, and then the general election, succeeding Ben Ray Lujan, who ran for the U.S. Senate. She took office in January 2021 and was re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

In Congress, she serves on the House Rules Committee and on the Natural Resources Committee, where she is ranking member of the Subcommittee on Indian and Insular Affairs; she chaired that subcommittee in the 117th Congress, when the STOP Act on trafficking of sacred cultural items passed.

She was elected chair of the Democratic Women's Caucus in 2024, co-chairs the National Labs, Rural Broadband and Historic Preservation caucuses and chairs the Head Start to Congress Caucus, according to her official biography, which also lists the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon Fire Assistance Act among her legislative work.
